extracted.intended_audience: community organisations, environmental defenders, policy advocates, lawyers and policymakers working on public participation and environmental/land/resource law in Kenya
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and submitting written memoranda, comments and submissions to national and county legislatures and regulatory bodies in Kenya on laws, regulations and policy instruments that affect communities (particularly in environmental, land, mining, water and extractives sectors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation must be effective quantitatively and qualitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation must be effective both quantitatively and qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislation being developed seeks to provide a framework to define the parameters for assessing effectiveness and the obligations of state organs and public offices when conducting public participation; effectiveness means not just numbers of participants but meaningful, substantive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative framework should define obligations and assessment parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws should provide a framework for public participation by defining the parameters for assessing its effectiveness and defining the obligations of state organs and public offices when conducting public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory framework helps prevent consultations from being treated as mere formality; submissions can push for clear duties, processes, timelines and accountability mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguity and vagueness in public participation law
rubrics_metrics.description: The current ambiguity and vagueness in the law allows duty bearers to conduct consultations as a formality; the law should prescribe requirements that meet the Constitutional threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should seek clear, unambiguous standards so public participation is substantive rather than perfunctory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active tracking and timely submission of memoranda
rubrics_metrics.description: Support communities by tracking notices and calls for public participation, and preparing and submitting written memoranda to Parliament and County Assemblies on laws that affect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advocacy involves monitoring legislative activity closely and ensuring written community input is submitted within consultation periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIA process must include a scoping report before full EIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Project proponents should complete a scoping report before undertaking the full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) study so that terms of reference can be finalised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of scoping affects finalisation of terms of reference and removes authority from NEMA to comment; submissions should press for mandatory scoping and clear process steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for classifying projects by risk must be clear and consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of projects into low-, medium- and high-risk for EIA purposes should be clear to avoid piecemeal amendments and arbitrary exemptions from full EIA studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose piecemeal regulatory changes that grant excessive discretion to authorities; insist on transparent criteria and safeguards against exemptions that bypass full assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations should be officially approved and gazetted
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations and amendments must be officially approved and published in the Kenyan Gazette to have legal effect and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and demand formal publication rather than relying on draft or piecemeal amendments that create legal uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative bodies must respond to access to information requests within 21 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Access to Information Act, administrative institutions must respond to information requests within the stipulated 21-day period; aggrieved parties can seek redress from the Commission on Administrative Justice (CAJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statutory complaint mechanism (CAJ) when responses are delayed or refused; submissions should seek regulations and institutional arrangements that make this right practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devolve CAJ functions to improve access to remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a clear need to devolve the office of the CAJ to better promote access to remedies when the right to information is unreasonably denied, particularly for marginalised communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for county-level offices or processes so communities can more readily enforce access to information rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information must be timely, affordable and meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: Information requested (including environmental information) should be accessible in a timely, less costly and meaningful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on access regulations, emphasise practical barriers communities face and propose measures (e.g., fee waivers, formats, outreach) to make information useable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove judicial oversight over government development projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that prevent a court from stopping any government development project once land acquisition is complete are constitutionality-problematic and should be deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions on land acquisition laws should insist that courts retain the power to grant relief and that judicial review remains available during acquisition processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit government possession of land before compensation is paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws should not allow the government to take possession of compulsorily acquired land before compensating affected individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose provisions that permit taking possession prior to payment or that permit long delays (e.g., up to one year) before compensation; insist on prompt, effective remedies and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise non-monetary/community values of land in compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuation approaches should recognise non-monetary values that communities attach to ancestral lands and not rely solely on a market value approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for compensation frameworks that account for cultural, livelihood and communal values to avoid unjust outcomes for communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-sharing laws must apportion monetary and non-monetary benefits to communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural resources benefit-sharing laws should apportion greater monetary and non-monetary benefits to communities and involve them in management of resources within their territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting submissions, push for clear mechanisms, timelines and institutional arrangements that guarantee community shares and management roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect rights to peaceful assembly and avoid strict liability for organisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments imposing strict liability on organisers of demonstrations for damage or injuries risk unconstitutionally limiting the right to peacefully assemble and may intimidate activists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should challenge provisions that unduly restrict civic space and propose alternatives that protect public order without curtailing constitutional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely compensation for wildlife damage and support local compensation committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Bills should specify timelines for payment of compensation (e.g., six months) for human death, injury, crop or property damage caused by wildlife, and allocate adequate facilities to County Wildlife Conservation and Compensation Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for enforceable timelines, clear procedures and resourcing so affected persons receive prompt remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fragmentation and ensure harmonisation of overlapping laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple bills or laws address similar issues (e.g., benefit-sharing), care must be taken to harmonise provisions to avoid fragmentation and conflicting protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should identify overlaps and request coherence across statutes and regulations to prevent gaps or contradictory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require environmentally friendly technology and safeguards in industry-specific laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectoral legislation (e.g., the Sugar Bill) should include mandatory obligations on industries to use environmentally friendly technologies due to social, economic and environmental impacts on nearby communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for mandatory environmental performance standards and technology requirements, not mere voluntary guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainstream environmental protection and safeguards in mining frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft mining policies, strategies and regulations must mainstream environmental protection and safeguards and promote just benefit-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions on mining instruments should ensure environmental safeguards are embedded across strategic plans, operational regulations and agreements with communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainstream gender and increase women's participation in extractive sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectoral strategies (e.g., Draft Gender Strategy for Mining) should address marginalisation of women along the value chain and create spaces, capacity and opportunities for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for concrete targets, capacity building, and institutional mechanisms to increase women’s participation and protect their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Development Agreements must be participatory and comprehensive
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic Community Development Agreement must include community consultations, engagement and participation; responsibilities and obligations of parties; code of conduct; project implementation; financial management and reporting requirements; and dispute and conflict resolution mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote use of model agreements and clear guidelines to ensure agreements are negotiated through participatory processes in line with constitutional principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote local equity and citizen participation in mining investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should ensure citizens participate in mineral resource development, acquire a stake in mining companies operating in Kenya and encourage local capital mobilisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for mechanisms (e.g., local equity rules, citizen shares, local fundraising incentives) that genuinely enable local ownership and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water regulations must ensure access, environmental protection and access to remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Water regulations should ensure access to a constant supply of water at national and county levels, protect the environment, include strict environmental protection mechanisms during licensing, and provide access to remedies when rights to a clean and healthy environment are threatened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should emphasise devolution of affordable water services, protection of natural sources from contamination and enforcement/monitoring provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory design must align with new institutional mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: When institutions and mandates change (e.g., Water Resources Authority, Basin Committees), regulations should be updated so rules align with the new institutional architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate that drafts explicitly reflect institutional roles, coordination mechanisms and accountability across levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict licensing, monitoring and public access in ozone-depleting substances regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations on substances that deplete the ozone layer should include strict licensing processes; effective monitoring of compliance with licence conditions; public access to license information; restriction of listed substances; and constant review of listed substances based on scientific findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push for transparent licensing records, robust monitoring/enforcement, and science-based, regularly updated substance lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forest management rules must enable community participation and prevent rights violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Forest (Community Participation in Sustainable Forest Management) Rules should provide for community participation in management, and clarify how authorisations (permits, licences, agreements, concessions) are applied for, granted, varied or cancelled, to avoid exclusionary conservation models and human rights violations (e.g., forced evictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should press for community management roles, clarity on authorisation processes and safeguards against abuse by agencies like the Kenya Forest Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: County regulations must be consistent with national law and ensure coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: County-level instruments (e.g., Kilifi Air Quality Regulations) must ensure consistency with the Environmental Management and Coordination Act (EMCA) and the Constitution, and enhance collaboration between county government, NEMA and affected communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for mechanisms for intergovernmental coordination, clarity on mandates and joint monitoring to ensure implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions should include constitutional/legal analysis where provisions appear unconstitutional
rubrics_metrics.description: When bills contain unconstitutional provisions (e.g., on assembly or land acquisition), submissions should explicitly raise those concerns in parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use constitutional arguments and cite jurisprudence and practical impacts to persuade legislators and committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in extractives: disclose licenses, contracts, beneficial owners and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency frameworks for petroleum/extractives should require disclosure of any petroleum license, contract, concession, production-sharing agreement, beneficial owners, exploration and production data, revenue collection, allocation and management, and social and environmental contributions and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on transparency frameworks, insist on comprehensive disclosures pre- and post-constitution, including beneficial ownership and impact data to enable public oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure participation mechanisms remain functional during emergencies (e.g., COVID-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Covid-19 pandemic limited spaces for civic engagement and participation; political goodwill and alternative participation channels are required to ensure communities remain able to influence the legislative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for contingency modalities (written submissions, digital hearings, extended timelines) and political commitment to preserve participation rights during emergencies.
